The worksheet itself is a blank record-keeping form with no filled-in sample figures.
text:
This source includes a simple farm bookkeeping worksheet (តារាងផែនការអាជីវកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ / តារាងវិភាគចំណូលចំណាយ) that a farmer can use, alongside a season's climate-adaptation planning, to record the costs and returns of a single rice-growing cycle. It is a blank template with no pre-filled numbers - farmers fill in their own local quantities and prices each season.

Expense side, recorded with columns for quantity, unit, unit price, and total cost:
1. Initial inputs (ចំណាយថ្លៃដើម): seed (ពូជស្រូវ, by kg), organic/manure fertilizer (ជីធម្មជាតិ, by sack/បាវ), chemical fertilizer (ជីគីមី, by kg), and fuel (ប្រេងសាំង, by liter).
2. Equipment and materials (ថ្លៃឧបករណ៍/សម្ភារៈ): irrigation pump hose (កូនពងទឹក, by count), sacks/bags (បាវ, by count), fertilizer-bag/container rental (ធ្នេជីកំប៉ុង, by sack), and draft-animal or plow equipment (គោយន្ត) - the form notes this last item is typically depreciated over a 2-year period rather than charged fully to one season.
3. Labor (ថ្លៃពលកម្ម): cost of labor for transplanting/weeding and general crop care, recorded per person-day (នាក់/ថ្ងៃ), covering hired and/or family labor time.

Income side:
4. Output achieved (ចំណូល - ផលិតផលដែលសម្រេចបាន): the quantity of rice actually harvested (បរិមាណផលស្រូវ, by kg), used to compute total production income.
5. Household use (ការប្រើប្រាស់ក្នុងគ្រួសារ): rice consumed at home (ស៊ីនៅផ្ទះ, by kg) and rice/broken-rice used as animal feed (ចំណីសត្វ / ចុងអង្ករ, by kg) - portions of the harvest that are not sold.
6. Seed reserved (បរិមាណស្រូវទុកពូជ): quantity of harvested rice set aside as seed stock for the next season (by kg).

Profit calculation, as laid out in the worksheet:
- Total production cost = initial inputs + equipment/materials + labor.
- Total profit (សរុបចំណេញ) = total production income − total production cost.
- Net profit (សរុបប្រាក់ចំណេញសុទ្ធ) = total profit − (household consumption + seed reserved), i.e. net profit accounts for the portion of the harvest kept for home use or as seed rather than sold.

Numeric precision caveat: no sample figures are given anywhere in this worksheet; all quantities, unit prices, and totals are meant to be filled in by the farmer using their own local costs and yields each season.
